passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch David’s house in order to kill him.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this song.
David gave it to the choirmaster.
David called the tune “Do Not Destroy.”
David wrote this as a Miktam.
Saul sent men to watch David’s house.
Saul wanted to kill David.

passages.text: Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise against me.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
Saul sent men to watch David’s house.
They wanted to kill David.
David prayed to God.
David said, “Deliver me from my enemies, O my God.”
David asked God to protect him from those who rise against him.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ אַל־ תַּשְׁחֵת֮ לְדָוִ֪ד מִ֫כְתָּ֥ם בִּשְׁלֹ֥חַ שָׁא֑וּל וַֽיִּשְׁמְר֥וּ אֶת־ הַ֝בַּ֗יִת לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃ הַצִּילֵ֖נִי מֵאֹיְבַ֥י׀ אֱלֹהָ֑י מִּמִתְקוֹמְמַ֥י תְּשַׂגְּבֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Deliver me from workers of iniquity, and save me from men of bloodshed.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David faces danger from evil people.
David asks God to deliver him from workers of iniquity.
David asks God to save him from men of bloodshed.
passages.original: הַ֭צִּילֵנִי מִפֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן וּֽמֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י דָ֝מִ֗ים הוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: See how they lie in wait for me. Fierce men conspire against me for no transgression or sin of my own, O LORD.
passages.sermon:
David speaks in this psalm.
David is innocent.
David has not sinned.
David has not done wrong.
Fierce men surround David.
These men wait to attack David.
They plan against David.
David calls to the LORD.
David says, "O LORD, see what they do."
David asks God to notice his innocence.
passages.original: כִּ֤י הִנֵּ֪ה אָֽרְב֡וּ לְנַפְשִׁ֗י יָג֣וּרוּ עָלַ֣י עַזִ֑ים לֹא־ פִשְׁעִ֖י וְלֹא־ חַטָּאתִ֣י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For no fault of my own, they move swiftly to attack me. Arise to help me, and take notice.
passages.sermon:
My enemies attack me quickly.
I have done nothing wrong.
They run toward me without cause.
God, wake up and come to help me.
Look at what is happening to me.
passages.original: בְּֽלִי־ עָ֭וֺן יְרוּצ֣וּן וְיִכּוֹנָ֑נוּ ע֖וּרָה לִקְרָאתִ֣י וּרְאֵה׃

passages.text: O LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God of Hosts.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
LORD, rise up.
Punish all the nations.
Do not show mercy to wicked traitors.
They come back in the evening.
They snarl like dogs.
They prowl around the city.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָֽה־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀ צְבָא֡וֹת אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הָקִ֗יצָה לִפְקֹ֥ד כָּֽל־ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם אַל־ תָּחֹ֨ן כָּל־ בֹּ֖גְדֵי אָ֣וֶן סֶֽלָה׃ יָשׁ֣וּבוּ לָ֭עֶרֶב יֶהֱמ֥וּ כַכָּ֗לֶב וִיס֥וֹבְבוּ עִֽיר׃

passages.text: See what they spew from their mouths— sharp words from their lips: “For who can hear us?”
passages.sermon:
Evil men attack me without cause.
They speak with their mouths.
They pour out sharp and harmful words.
Their lips bring forth words like swords.
They say, “Who can hear us?”
They believe no one listens to them.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה׀ יַבִּ֘יע֤וּן בְּפִיהֶ֗ם חֲ֭רָבוֹת בְּשִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם כִּי־ מִ֥י שֹׁמֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations.
passages.sermon: The LORD is God.\r\nThe LORD laughs at them.\r\nThe LORD mocks all the nations.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תִּשְׂחַק־ לָ֑מוֹ תִּ֝לְעַ֗ג לְכָל־ גּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: I will keep watch for You, O my strength, because You, O God, are my fortress.
passages.sermon: God is my strength.\r\nGod is my fortress.\r\nI will keep watch for God.
passages.original: עֻ֭זּוֹ אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֶשְׁמֹ֑רָה כִּֽי־ אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים מִשְׂגַּבִּֽי׃

passages.text: My God of loving devotion will come to meet me; God will let me stare down my foes.
passages.sermon:
God shows loving devotion.
God comes to meet me.
God lets me see my enemies.
God lets me look at those who oppose me.
passages.original: אֱלֹהֵ֣י חַסְדּוֹ יְקַדְּמֵ֑נִי אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים יַרְאֵ֥נִי בְשֹׁרְרָֽי׃

passages.text: Do not kill them, or my people will forget. Scatter them by Your power, and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.
passages.sermon:
God is the shield and protector of His people.
Do not kill these enemies.
If You kill them, my people will forget.
Scatter these enemies with Your power.
Bring them down, Lord, our shield.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּהַרְגֵ֤ם׀ פֶּֽן־ יִשְׁכְּח֬וּ עַמִּ֗י הֲנִיעֵ֣מוֹ בְ֭חֵילְךָ וְהוֹרִידֵ֑מוֹ מָֽגִנֵּ֣נוּ אֲדֹנָֽי׃

passages.text: By the sins of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be trapped in their pride, in the curses and lies they utter.
passages.sermon:
They sin with their mouths.
They speak wrong words with their lips.
Let them become trapped by their pride.
They tell curses.
They speak lies.
passages.original: חַטַּאת־ פִּ֗ימוֹ דְּֽבַר־ שְׂפָ֫תֵ֥ימוֹ וְיִלָּכְד֥וּ בִגְאוֹנָ֑ם וּמֵאָלָ֖ה וּמִכַּ֣חַשׁ יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more, so it may be known to the ends of the earth that God rules over Jacob. Selah They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
passages.sermon:
God rules over Jacob.
God rules to the ends of the earth.
God acts with power and authority.
God is the judge.
God consumes the wicked in His wrath.
God destroys them until they are gone.
People everywhere will know God rules.
In the evening, the wicked return.
They snarl like dogs.
They prowl around the city.
passages.original: כַּלֵּ֥ה בְחֵמָה֮ כַּלֵּ֪ה וְֽאֵ֫ינֵ֥מוֹ וְֽיֵדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־ אֱ֭לֹהִים מֹשֵׁ֣ל בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב לְאַפְסֵ֖י הָאָ֣רֶץ סֶֽלָה׃ וְיָשׁ֣וּבוּ לָ֭עֶרֶב יֶהֱמ֥וּ כַכָּ֗לֶב וִיס֥וֹבְבוּ עִֽיר׃

passages.text: They scavenge for food, and growl if they are not satisfied.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David fought against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah.
Joab struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
David describes his enemies.
They wander around to find food.
They do not stop searching for something to eat.
If they are not satisfied, they growl.
They complain when they are still hungry.
passages.original: הֵ֭מָּה יְנוּעוּן לֶאֱכֹ֑ל אִם־ לֹ֥א יִ֝שְׂבְּע֗וּ וַיָּלִֽינוּ׃

passages.text: But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning. For You are my fortress, my refuge in times of trouble.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David says, “I will sing about Your strength.”
David says, “I will praise Your loving devotion in the morning.”
David says, “You are my fortress.”
David says, “You are my refuge in times of trouble.”
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י׀ אָשִׁ֣יר עֻזֶּךָ֮ וַאֲרַנֵּ֥ן לַבֹּ֗קֶר חַ֫סְדֶּ֥ךָ כִּֽי־ הָיִ֣יתָ מִשְׂגָּ֣ב לִ֑י וּ֝מָנ֗וֹס בְּי֣וֹם צַר־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: To You, O my strength, I sing praises, for You, O God, are my fortress, my God of loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David calls God his strength.
David sings praises to God.
God is David’s fortress.
God is the God of loving devotion.
passages.original: עֻ֭זִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֲזַמֵּ֑רָה כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י אֱלֹהֵ֥י חַסְדִּֽי׃
